title: Lesson 56: Localization and Multi-Currency Architecture: Locale, Language, and Dated Exchange Rates
description: Separating locale from language, setting org and user defaults, and using multi-currency with dated exchange rates to keep one org correct across many countries.

questions.question: Two users read an interface in the same language but have different locales. What differs on their screens?
options: Only the words on the buttons, because the interface language governs everything
The date, time, and number formatting, even though the language is the same
Nothing, because locale and language always change together
Every amount's currency, which is rebuilt for each user's region
questions.explanation: Language controls the words on the interface, while locale controls how values are shaped: dates, times, numbers, names, and addresses. With the same language, users with different locales still see different value formats.

questions.question: With advanced currency management enabled, which conversion does NOT use the dated exchange rate?
options: An opportunity that closed in a month whose rate is on record
An opportunity product line item amount
A currency formula field result on the opportunity
A report on opportunities that shows the converted amount
questions.explanation: Dated exchange rates apply to opportunities and their related objects and reports, but not to currency formula fields, forecasting, currency fields on other objects, or cross-object formulas, which fall back to static conversion.

questions.question: An account's default currency is changed from one currency to another. What happens to its existing amounts?
options: They are not converted, just shown with the new currency code
They are immediately revalued at the current exchange rate
They are converted to the corporate currency and back again
The change is blocked until advanced currency management is on
questions.explanation: Changing a record's default currency does not revalue its amounts; it only changes the currency code they display with. Revaluation is a separate, deliberate operation, not a side effect of the label change.
